newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Redland H1 profits seen sliding.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Redland H1 profits seen sliding.

text.p: Redland Plc, the UK building materials group, is expected to announce a sharp slide in half year pretax profits next Thursday and freeze the interim dividend payout at last year's level, after a difficult period, particularly in Germany.

Interim pretax profits are expected to be between 86 million stg and 130 million, a steep fall from last year's 165.2 million, according to analysts' forecasts. The company, like others in the sector, has been hit by bad weather at the year-start delaying building plus very weak markets.
The dividend is expected to be frozen at last year's 5.5 pence. Redland is another building materials group which is dependent on the German market for much of its profits.

Earlier this week rival RMC Group Plc, another German-dependent player, reported a collapse in its profits because of difficulties in that particular market. It warned that the problems could extend into 1997.

Simon Brown, the analyst at UBS who sees Redland pretax profits of 130 million, said "I would anticipate a relatively cautious statement from Redland on Germany as well, but a more upbeat outlook on the recent reorganisation."
The results will be the first after Redland announced a deal with Germany's Braas GmbH to create a new roof tile business called Redland Braas.
That deal makes the merged unit the biggest player in Europe and was unveiled in the Spring. Analysts expect an update and say the results will give a taster of how the operation has been going.

Another analyst, who is predicting profits of 110 million, said he thought it was too early for a clear view of the success of Redland Braas but he added he expected the update to show a more mixed picture on Germany.
"The German situation is a case of steadier growth in the West and problems in the East."
